content: 1. The concurrent use of stiripentol with other central nervous system (CNS) depressants, including alcohol, may elevate the risk of sedation and somnolence. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Succinylcholine enhances cholinergic effects/transmission, while meclizine reduces them. The clinical impact of this interaction is unclear; therefore, caution is advised. 3. Meclizine and sufentanil both potentiate sedation. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 4. Meclizine and sufentanil sublingual formulations both increase sedation. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 5. Meclizine and suvorexant both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Meclizine and tapentadol both increase sedation. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 7. Meclizine and tasimelteon both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Meclizine and temazepam both increase sedation. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 9. Meclizine and tetrabenazine both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Meclizine reduces the levels of thioridazine by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Additionally, meclizine decreases thioridazine levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism, while thioridazine increases the effects of meclizine via pharmacodynamic synergism. Both agents also increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Meclizine reduces the levels of thiothixene by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Meclizine also decreases thiothixene levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism, while thiothixene increases the effects of meclizine via pharmacodynamic synergism. Both agents enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Meclizine and tiagabine both increase sedation. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 13. Meclizine and tiotropium both reduce cholinergic effects/transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Meclizine and tizanidine both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Meclizine and tolcapone both increase sedation. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 16. Meclizine and tolterodine both reduce cholinergic effects/transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Meclizine and topiramate both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Meclizine and tramadol both increase sedation. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 19. Meclizine and trazodone both reduce cholinergic effects/transmission and increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Meclizine and triazolam both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Meclizine reduces the levels of trifluoperazine by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Meclizine also decreases trifluoperazine levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism, while trifluoperazine increases the effects of meclizine via pharmacodynamic synergism. Both agents enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Meclizine and trihexyphenidyl both reduce cholinergic effects/transmission. There is potential for additive anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Meclizine and trimipramine both reduce cholinergic effects/transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Meclizine and triprolidine both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Meclizine and trospium chloride both reduce cholinergic effects/transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Meclizine and valproic acid both increase sedation. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 27. Meclizine and vecuronium both reduce cholinergic effects/transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Meclizine and vigabatrin both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Meclizine and zaleplon both increase sedation. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 30. Meclizine and ziconotide both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Meclizine reduces the levels of ziprasidone by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Meclizine also decreases ziprasidone levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism, while ziprasidone increases the effects of meclizine via pharmacodynamic synergism. Both agents enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Meclizine and zolpidem both increase sedation. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 33. Meclizine and zonisamide both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Meclizine reduces the levels of zotepine by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Meclizine also decreases zotepine levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Meclizine may mask the ototoxicity of aminoglycosides such as amikacin, gentamicin, neomycin, paromomycin, streptomycin, and tobramycin. The mechanism of interaction is unspecified, and the clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 36. Meclizine increases the levels of digoxin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 37. Dimenhydrinate increases the toxicity of meclizine via pharmacodynamic synergism. Additive anticholinergic effects may occur. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 38. Donepezil and galantamine reduce the effects of meclizine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 39. Meclizine increases the effects of abobotulinumtoxinA via pharmacodynamic synergism. Drugs with anticholinergic effects may potentiate botulinum toxin effects, leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. Monitor closely. 40. Meclizine and acetaminophen/phenyltoxamine both enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Meclizine and aclidinium both reduce cholinergic effects/transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Meclizine and acrivastine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Meclizine and alfentanil both enhance sedation. Avoid or use alternative drugs unless no other treatment options are available. Monitor closely. 44. Meclizine and alprazolam both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Meclizine and amantadine may result in increased anticholinergic adverse effects due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Meclizine increases the toxicity of amifampridine. Amifampridine can cause seizures, and coadministration with drugs that lower the seizure threshold may heighten this risk. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 47. Meclizine and amisulpride both enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Meclizine and amitriptyline both reduce cholinergic effects/transmission and increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Meclizine and amobarbital both enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Meclizine and amoxapine both reduce cholinergic effects/transmission and increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Meclizine and anticholinergic/sedative combinations both reduce cholinergic effects/transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Meclizine reduces the levels of aripiprazole by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Meclizine also decreases aripiprazole levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism, while aripiprazole increases the effects of meclizine via pharmacodynamic synergism. Both agents enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Meclizine and asenapine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Meclizine and atracurium both reduce cholinergic effects/transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Meclizine and atropine both reduce cholinergic effects/transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Meclizine and avapritinib both enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Meclizine and baclofen both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Meclizine and belladonna alkaloids both reduce cholinergic effects/transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Meclizine and benperidol both reduce cholinergic effects/transmission. Additive anticholinergic effects and possible hypoglycemia may occur. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Meclizine and benzodiazepines such as alprazolam, clonazepam, and chlordiazepoxide both enhance sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Meclizine and codeine both increase sedation. Avoid or use alternative drugs unless no other treatment options are available. Monitor closely. 62. Meclizine and cyclobenzaprine both reduce cholinergic effects/transmission and increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Meclizine and daridorexant both increase the risk of CNS depression, potentially leading to additive psychomotor impairment and daytime dysfunction. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
